extracted.intended_audience: ACUS staff, consultants, committee members, administrative law stakeholders and members of the public involved in or following ACUS rulemaking/recommendation processes
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the official ACUS process for developing, approving, and implementing Recommendations and for adopting Statements as an alternative output. Covers roles (Office of the Chairman, consultants, committees, Council, Assembly), report preparation, approval steps, and implementation obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main statutory function of ACUS
rubrics_metrics.description: The main statutory function of ACUS is to bring together the public and private sectors to recommend improvements to administrative and regulatory processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This frames ACUS’s purpose and should guide what topics and outputs (Recommendations/Statements) are appropriate; projects should aim to identify and recommend improvements to administrative/regulatory procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement of consultants or in‑house staff
rubrics_metrics.description: ACUS’s Office of the Chairman, with the approval of the Council, engages consultants to study administrative processes or procedures that may need improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement requires Office of the Chairman action and Council approval; work may be performed by external consultants or in‑house staff and should focus on processes/procedures needing improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of a comprehensive research report proposing recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultants or in‑house staff then prepare a comprehensive research report proposing recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should be comprehensive and include proposed recommendations. The report is the basis for committee discussion and drafting of Recommendations; quality and completeness of the report are central to advancing through the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee discussion and drafting of a Recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: An ACUS committee discusses this report, preparing a draft Recommendation to submit to the Council and, with approval, to the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee deliberation should evaluate the research report and translate findings into a draft Recommendation suitable for Council review; drafting should follow ACUS norms and produce a document ready for Council consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council approval and Assembly adoption following debate
rubrics_metrics.description: Following a debate the Assembly adopts the final Recommendation, which ACUS undertakes to implement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval is a multi‑step governance process: Council approval is required to forward a draft to the Assembly; the Assembly debates and adopts the final Recommendation. Adoption carries an obligation (or commitment) by ACUS to undertake implementation activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Statements as alternative to formal Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: On occasion, the ACUS membership has acted to adopt a “Statement” to express its views on a particular matter without making a formal recommendation on the subject. ACUS statements are typically the product of the same process that leads to recommendations, but may set forth issues, conclusions from a study, or comments, rather than recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements follow substantially the same procedural path as Recommendations but differ in form and function: they express views, issues, conclusions, or comments rather than prescriptive recommendations. Use a Statement when the objective is to record conclusions or commentary rather than to issue an implementable recommendation.
